metadata.methods_description: Subdural grid and strip electrodes (ADTECH, 10 mm inter-contact spacing) were implanted for pre-surgical evaluation. Video-EEG was recorded with a Micromed Brain-Quick System Evolution at 1024 Hz. CSD was computed by the data authors at four cortical sites (Fl1, Fl2, iP, Fb). The associated paper describes 1-30 Hz Butterworth filtering and rank normalization, but the source deposit does not state whether the stored values are before or after these steps. Each segment contains 20480 samples across 4 channels.

citation_details.title: Genes Encoding Small Heat Shock Proteins of the Silkworm,Bombyx mori
citation_details.author: Daisuke Sakano, Bin Li, Qingyou Xia, Kohji Yamamoto, Hiroshi Fujii, Yoichi Aso
citation_details.abstract: Small heat shock protein (sHSP) is a family of ubiquitous polypeptides involved in a variety of physiological phenomena. From the silkworm, Bombyx mori, we isolated and sequenced the following cDNAs encoding sHSPs: shsp19.9, shsp20.1, shsp20.4, shsp20.8, shsp21.4, and shsp23.7. shsp21.4 was nearly twice as large in size as other shsps. The deduced amino acid sequence of sHSP21.4 was similar to that of Drosophila melanogaster CG14207-PA. Other sHSPs were highly similar to each other and, in a phylogenetic tree, formed a cluster including Plodia interpunctella alphaCP25. It was speculated that shsp21.4 has at least one intron in genome while other shsps do not. The transcripts of all shsps were subtle, but were constitutively detected in various tissues. Heat shock triggered a substantial increase in the transcripts other than shsp21.4. The B. mori sHSPs are perhaps classified into at least two groups: sHSP21.4 and others.
